podcast.body: Critic Greal Marcus cited "Superstition" as a prime example of the powerful and distinctive black music that became widely heard on radio in the early 1970s, noting that such songs, which would have been curiosities just a year prior, now formed a coherent musical statement. "Stevie Wonder's superstition only a year before such songs would have been a curiosity."

srcs.episode: Ep. 22 - Power to the People - The Music of the Black Power Movement

podcast.body: The song "Superstition" was composed and recorded by Stevie Wonder using the TONTO synthesizer, in collaboration with Malcolm Cecil and Robert Margouleff. It is highlighted as one of the very important records from the 1970s that came out of this partnership. "Just like superstition, living for the city, boogie on reggae woman, higher ground, and many others were all composed and recorded using Tonto."
